Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems.

Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines.

Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges.

Job Purpose

The Product Owner owns the backlog and roadmap for GSK's perimeter security product, translating what GSK teams need into prioritised work and maximising the value the platform delivers to the teams that consume it. The role works daily with engineering to deliver increments and accept completed work, links every backlog item to strategy and OKRs, and measures adoption and outcome rather than output.

The role sits inside the platform team and holds genuine product decision rights over backlog order and acceptance. Platform strategy and the multi-year roadmap sit with the Platform Manager, domain demand and sequencing sit with the Domain Portfolio Manager, technical design and standards sit with the Platform Architect, and the reliability bar sits with Reliability Engineering.

Key Responsibilities

Own and prioritise the product backlog by value, risk and reliability, applying lean portfolio principles rather than fixed project plans.
Link every backlog item explicitly to GSK D&T strategy and domain OKRs, and measure the outcome with a named metric.
Translate consumer needs and business outcomes into clear requirements and user stories that engineering can act on without further interpretation.
Work daily with the engineering team through refinement, planning and review, and accept completed increments against agreed criteria.
Balance new capability against the reliability bar, agreeing SLOs and error budget impact with Reliability Engineering before committing to work.
Use AI tooling to accelerate discovery, backlog refinement and requirement drafting, and record where AI-assisted output has been reviewed before acceptance.
Measure product adoption, self-service uptake and value delivered, and iterate the roadmap on that evidence rather than on stakeholder volume.
Steer delivery with flow metrics such as throughput, cycle time and work in progress, and act on them rather than reporting them.
Manage consumer demand and stakeholder expectations, saying no with a reason where an item does not compete on value.
Manage supplier-delivered components within the product, holding partners to the same acceptance criteria and reliability standards as internal work.
Contribute the product view into the domain roadmap held by the Platform Manager and the portfolio view held by the Domain Portfolio Manager.
Hold the boundaries with the Platform Manager on platform strategy, the Platform Architect on technical design and standards, and Reliability Engineering on the reliability bar.

Product ownership in a platform or agile environment, covering backlog management, prioritisation and increment acceptance.
Outcome measurement, covering OKRs, adoption metrics and flow metrics used to steer delivery.

Experience Required

Overall 15 years and typically 5 or more years in product ownership or product management, including at least two years owning a backlog in a platform or infrastructure context.
Practical experience of lean or agile backlog management, including prioritisation by value and risk rather than by request order.
Track record of translating business needs into requirements that engineering teams could deliver without repeated clarification.
Experience working to OKRs and measuring adoption or value delivered rather than features shipped.
Experience steering with flow metrics and acting on delivery predictability data.
Experience managing stakeholders and declining requests with a defensible reason.
Exposure to AI tooling used for discovery, backlog refinement or requirement drafting.
Experience delivering perimeter security capabilities as a Product Owner or equivalent member of an Agile team.
Capability in Team Backlog prioritisation, story definition, acceptance criteria, Planning Interval events and iteration execution.
Evidence of delivering perimeter improvements that reduced risk, improved control coverage or simplified secure access.

Decisiveness on backlog order, including the confidence to sequence against value rather than seniority of the requester.
Clear written communication, since requirements and acceptance criteria are the role's primary output.
Enough technical literacy to challenge engineering estimates and understand reliability trade-offs.
Comfort with data as the basis for roadmap change rather than stakeholder pressure.
Collaborative habit with architecture and reliability colleagues who can veto on standards grounds.

jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
About Us

HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.

To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.

Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

OUR PEOPLE

With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

OUR IMPACT

Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We're proud to be a part of that.

About The Team

The B2C/Creators Product team at HighLevel is focused on building and scaling a world-class learning experience for our customers and their audiences. The platform currently serves over 1.1 million monthly active users, making it one of HighLevel's most widely adopted products. This role offers a unique opportunity to operate at scale while solving B2C-style learner experience problems within a B2B2C product ecosystem.

Events is one of the newest products in HighLevel's Memberships suite, currently in beta and being built from the ground up. It gives our customers a native way to create, publish and sell events — in-person, online and hybrid — with ticketing, RSVPs, paid and free registration, and attendee management, sitting directly alongside the contacts, communities, courses, credentials and automations they already run their business on. Organizers build and run their events from the Memberships admin; attendees live the whole thing inside Client Portal, next to the courses, communities and credentials they already sign in for.

What You'll Do

Own and Shape the B2C & Events Roadmap Partner with product leadership to help shape and execute the roadmap for HighLevel's B2C platform, serving 1.1M+ monthly active learners, with a focus on engagement, completion, and retention in a B2B2C environment. 
Close the Table-Stakes Gap, Then Go Past It – Know the category cold. Get the expected capabilities right — ticket tiers, promo codes, capacity and waitlists, recurring and series events, refunds, embeddable widgets, calendar sync, wallet passes — and then decide deliberately where we go further than the incumbents rather than matching them feature for feature. 
Take Events from Beta to GA – Own the beta exit criteria: the quality bar, the reliability bar, the feature completeness, and the adoption and revenue signals that tell us this product is ready to be sold broadly. Drive the program that closes those gaps. 
Build Ticketing, Checkout and Payments – Lead paid, free and RSVP event types, multi-tier and multi-currency ticketing, checkout conversion, discounts, taxes, refunds and payouts — with the precision and trust a revenue-bearing flow demands, and with fee and payout terms that are a reason to choose us rather than a reason to resent us. 
Give Organizers Ownership of Their Audience – Build the capability that most defines us against the category: every registration flows into the organizer's own CRM, segmentable, automatable and theirs to keep. Turn attendee data ownership from a talking point into the product's most obvious advantage. 
Own Event-Day Operations – Events are judged on the day they happen. Own check-in and QR scanning, offline resilience at the door, guest lists and comp tickets, on-site sales, capacity enforcement and the operational tooling organizers depend on when things go wrong in real time. 
Own the Attendee Experience in Client Portal – Client Portal is where the attendee side of Events lives, and you own it: how members find what is on, register and check out, hold their tickets, receive reminders and joining links, attend in person or online, and look back at what they have been to. Deliver that journey across both web and mobile, make events feel native to the portal rather than bolted onto it, and hold a phone-first bar throughout. 
Drive Distribution and Discovery – Shape how events get found and filled: SEO-ready event pages, social and calendar syndication, embeddable listings, the Gokollab Marketplace, and the promotion tooling that turns an organizer's existing audience into attendance. 
Open the Platform – Treat APIs, webhooks and integrations as a first-class surface rather than a premium upsell, so agencies and developers can build events into the workflows and client solutions they already sell. 
Champion UI/UX Excellence – Partner closely with design and engineering to deliver interfaces that are intuitive, accessible, mobile-friendly and fast — for both the organizer building an event and the attendee registering for one. 
Talk to Organizers Constantly – Run discovery with beta organizers, sit in on their setup, watch where they stall, and turn qualitative signal into a prioritized backlog. At this stage, direct customer contact is a primary input, not a supplement. 
Experiment and Optimize – Design and analyze experiments across the funnel — event page conversion, registration completion, checkout drop-off, organizer onboarding — and iterate rapidly on evidence rather than opinion. 
Support Scale, Reliability and Trust – Drive the platform work a live-event product demands: registration integrity, capacity and waitlist correctness, payment reliability, fraud and listing trust, and graceful behavior under the traffic spikes that come with a popular event going on sale. 
Collaborate Cross-Functionally – Work across engineering, design, data, support, marketing and customer-facing teams to launch features, drive adoption, and close the loop on organizer feedback. 
Define and Own the Metrics – Establish the success metrics for a product that does not yet have them — organizer activation, time to first published event, repeat-event rate, registration and checkout conversion, attendance rate, gross ticket volume and revenue per organizer — set the OKRs against them, and use them to steer the roadmap. 
Deliver Outcomes, Not Just Features – Be accountable for measurable growth in events published, organizers activated, registrations processed and ticket revenue running through the platform. 

Who You Are

B2C Experience – You have built and shipped impactful features for B2C platforms or content products, creating engaging end user experiences that drive activation, completion, and retention at meaningful scale. 
An End-to-End Owner – You are comfortable owning the entire life of an event across two connected surfaces: the creator experience in the Memberships admin, where an organizer builds, prices, publishes, promotes and runs their event, and the attendee experience in Client Portal, where a member discovers it, registers, attends and looks back on it. You think in terms of the whole journey and the handoffs between those surfaces, not in terms of screens. 
UX-Attentive for Learning – You bring a strong UI/UX sensibility focused on learner journeys, content discovery, progress tracking, and habit formation, with a track record of delivering intuitive and high-quality learning experiences.

Job Description

The Global Risk & Compliance team is seeking a highly motivated Associate, Digital Product Management to join the Financial Crimes Products & Capabilities team and support several high-impact modernization initiatives.

In this role, you will help advance critical capabilities across Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) journeys, including the modernization of our Customer Risk Rating engine, development of our data strategy, and broader enterprise transformation efforts. You will work across Product, Technology, Compliance, and Data teams to strengthen American Express' Financial Crimes capabilities and help build scalable, modern platforms that support our risk management objectives.

Responsibilities

As an Associate, you will help deliver the modernization of enterprise wide KYC platform, support legacy system decommissioning, and contribute to the development of a unified data layer that will serve as a foundation for Financial Crimes platforms.

You will partner closely with teams across Lines of Business, Compliance, Data Governance, Platforms, and Technology to align priorities and execute modernization roadmaps.

Key Responsibilities Include

Translate business needs and requirements into clearly defined product capabilities, features, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
Manage and prioritize the product backlog in partnership with Product, Technology, and business stakeholders.
Drive alignment across stakeholders on product, delivery, and data decisions, balancing trade-offs, dependencies, and enterprise impact.
Participate actively in Agile ceremonies and partner with cross-functional teams to identify challenges, evaluate solutions, and support successful delivery.
Analyze data, query data sets, and develop data mapping specifications to support system integrations, migrations, and data sourcing requirements.
Partner with use-case owners and stakeholders to deliver end-to-end products and capabilities while identifying opportunities, dependencies, and gaps.
Support legacy platform decommissioning and modernization roadmaps, including milestone and dependency tracking.
Facilitate cross-functional working sessions, document decisions, and ensure clear ownership and follow-through on action items.
Support multi-market rollout coordination, including international expansion of high-risk KYC Refresh capabilities.
Communicate the value, progress, and impact of shared platform capabilities to leadership and partner teams.

Ways of Working

jobs.sourceTitle: Senior Product Manager – Data, Analytics & AI
jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
Company Background

Azuga, a Bridgestone company, is a leading global connected vehicle platform, helping customers turn data from vehicles and drivers into intelligence that improves operations and safety while reducing cost and risk. Azuga provides innovative end-to-end fleet solutions for commercial fleets, government agencies, insurance companies, and integrated software partners, through a comprehensive approach of hardware technology, fleet management applications, video telematics, and data analytics. All with a white glove customer experience.

Team Culture

We are a mission-driven team committed to remaining the fastest growing fleet management solution in the industry. We are a group of builders and doers — building the foundations of a results-oriented product team to deliver amazing experiences for our customers. We are a team with a strong commitment to customer-driven innovation, data-based decision making, and a bias for learning through experimentation.

Summary

Data is at the core of what Azuga does — every device in the field generates a continuous stream of signals that our customers depend on to run safer, smarter fleets. We are seeking a Senior Product Manager, Data, Analytics & AI to own the strategy and roadmap for how we collect, process, model, and surface that intelligence across the platform — and to help lead our emerging AI program from early initiative into a core platform capability.

This is a rare hybrid role. You will need to be equally comfortable in a technical conversation about data pipelines and model outputs as you are in a boardroom discussion about business outcomes and strategic direction. You will translate between two worlds — turning ambiguous business problems into clear technical requirements, and turning complex data and AI capabilities into intuitive, high-impact product experiences. You will work closely with engineering, data science, Sales, Customer Success, and executive leadership alike.

What You’ll Own

Data Ingestion & Pipeline Integrity

Own product requirements for how vehicle signals and driver events are collected, validated, and processed — from hardware in the field through to the data layer.
Define standards for data quality, completeness, and reliability in partnership with Engineering and Data Engineering, and ensure the infrastructure scales as fleet size and signal diversity grow.
Analytics & Insights Products

Own the roadmap for Azuga’s fleet analytics surfaces — dashboards, reports, trend analysis, and alert-driven insights — ensuring they are accurate, fast, and genuinely useful to fleet managers.
Define and evolve the metrics layer: what gets measured, how it’s calculated, and how it maps to customer outcomes like safety, efficiency, and cost reduction.
AI Program — Vision & Execution

Help lead Azuga’s AI program as it matures from a set of experiments into a standardized platform capability — owning the vision, roadmap, and delivery framework that makes AI a reliable, scalable part of the product.
Establish the infrastructure, data access patterns, and UX standards that allow AI features to be built and iterated consistently across the platform.
Define and track leading indicators of AI program health — such as recommendation acceptance rates and feature engagement — to measure real-world impact and guide investment decisions.
Serve as the product interface for data science and ML initiatives: framing problem statements, scoping features around model outputs, and ensuring AI-driven capabilities are explainable, trustworthy, and tied to measurable customer value.
Data APIs & Cross-Functional Translation

Define product requirements for external data APIs, ensuring Azuga’s data is accessible and reliable for partners and integrated software vendors.
Act as the connective tissue between technical and non-technical stakeholders — synthesizing inputs from Sales, Support, and executive leadership into a coherent product direction, and producing clear, detailed requirements that engineering teams can execute without ambiguity.
Key Responsibilities

Define and drive the data, analytics, and AI product roadmap, balancing near-term customer pain points against longer-term platform investment.
Lead product discovery across customer segments, translating feedback, usage data, and support escalations into prioritized requirements.
Write rigorous product requirements and user stories; partner with engineering and data science through the full development lifecycle.
Build trusted relationships with stakeholders across Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, and executive leadership — communicating clearly and managing expectations proactively.
Establish and monitor KPIs for data quality, analytics engagement, AI feature adoption, and API reliability.
Lead go-to-market planning and enablement for new analytics and AI feature launches.
Qualifications

5+ years of product management experience, with meaningful focus on data, analytics, or AI/ML products in B2B SaaS environments.
Demonstrated ability to translate between business requirements and technical specifications — comfortable in a data engineering standup and a Sales QBR in the same day.
Working fluency with data concepts: pipelines, schemas, APIs, event-driven architectures, and data quality frameworks. You don’t need to code, but you need to reason about tradeoffs at the technical level.
Experience working directly with data science or ML teams — defining problem statements, scoping features around model outputs, and making those outputs useful to end users.
High attention to detail — you write requirements that leave nothing ambiguous, and you catch the inconsistency others miss.
Excellent communicator with a track record of earning trust with engineers, data scientists, and executive stakeholders alike.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Business Analytics, or a related field; advanced degree is a plus.
Nice to Have

Background in fleet management, telematics, connected devices, or mobility/transportation.
Hands-on experience with BI platform product development (Looker, Tableau, or similar).
Familiarity with IoT data architectures, streaming pipelines, or AI-assisted prototyping workflows.
Join us at Azuga

This is a high-impact role at a company where data is the product and AI is the next frontier. You will own a domain that touches every fleet customer we serve and help shape how intelligence gets woven into everything Azuga does. If you find equal satisfaction in a cleanly defined schema and a well-told customer story — and thrive connecting those two things — we would love to hear from you.

About Us

We are a global climate technologies company engineered for sustainability. We create sustainable and efficient residential, commercial and industrial spaces through HVACR technologies. We protect temperature-sensitive goods throughout the cold chain. And we bring comfort to people globally. Best-in-class engineering, design and manufacturing combined with category-leading brands in compression, controls, software and monitoring solutions result in next-generation climate technology that is built for the needs of the world ahead. 

Whether you are a professional looking for a career change, an undergraduate student exploring your first opportunity, or recent graduate with an advanced degree, we have opportunities that will allow you to innovate, be challenged and make an impact. Join our team and start your journey today!

Overview

The Product Manager owns the entire product lifecycle, from conceptualization to obsolescence, defining what to build by translating market and customer needs into solutions that deliver profitable growth and competitive differentiation. This role is responsible for developing product roadmaps, managing product P&L, and ensuring alignment with customer needs and market opportunities. The Product Manager partners cross-functionally to deliver and maintain innovative, high-impact products that meet business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and execute 5-year product roadmaps, managing the product lifecycle from development to obsolescence
Set product priorities for new developments and manage product P&L to optimize margins
Create comprehensive business cases outlining expected returns
Define product positioning and ensure designs meet customer use cases
Owns and accurately maintains product information throughout the lifecycle
Gather and analyze Voice of Customer insights to inform product features and functionality
Translate market and customer insights into clear product requirements, features, and technical direction
Balance growth, cost, and profitability through disciplined product portfolio and lifecycle management
Own product data integrity and structure, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and alignment with global data standards to enable effective commercialization, analytics, and digital tools
Support pricing strategy and execution by providing product inputs (e.g., cost, features, value drivers) and partnering with Pricing to enable value-based pricing, margin optimization, and competitive positioning
Develop and support sales enablement tools (e.g., product documentation, technical collateral, value drivers) to ensure accurate representation of product capabilities and effective customer engagement
Partner cross-functionally (engineering, operations, commercial) to ensure successful delivery and adoption
Continuously refine products based on performance, feedback, and evolving customer needs

KPIs

Revenue and profitability by product line 
Market share growth vs. competitors 
ROI on new product development 
Roadmap execution (on-time, in-scope delivery) 
Customer satisfaction and product adoption 

Required Qualifications

Minimum five years of experience in product management, product development, or a related field.
Proven leadership and communication skills with success in aligning cross-functional teams to deliver product roadmaps and achieve revenue goals.
Advanced proficiency with product lifecycle management tools, data analysis platforms, and performance tracking systems.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills rooted in data-driven decision-making and customer-centric product development.
A relentless pursuit of excellence and a strong desire to build innovative products that deliver profitable growth and competitive differentiation.
Deep commitment to ownership, continuous learning, and taking proactive steps to improve product outcomes.

Preferred Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, engineering, marketing, or a related field.
Advanced knowledge of product positioning, pricing strategies, and P&L management.
Experience in developing business cases, ROI analysis, and product roadmaps.
Deep understanding of Voice of Customer (VoC) insights, translating into product requirements.
Familiarity with agile development methodologies and tools.

Our Commitment to Our People

Across the globe, we are united by a singular Purpose: Sustainability is no small ambition. That’s why everything we do is geared toward a sustainable future—for our generation and all those to come. Through groundbreaking innovations, HVACR technology and cold chain solutions, we are reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency in spaces of all sizes, from residential to commercial to industrial.

Our employees are our greatest strength. We believe that our culture of passion, openness, and collaboration empowers us to work toward the same goal - to make the world a better place. We invest in the end-to-end development of our people, beginning at onboarding and through senior leadership, so they can thrive personally and professionally.

Flexible and competitive benefits plans offer the right options to meet your individual/family needs. We provide employees with flexible time off plans, including paid parental leave (maternal and paternal), vacation and holiday leave. 

Together, we have the opportunity – and the power – to continue to revolutionize the technology behind air conditioning, heating and refrigeration, and cultivate a better future. Learn more about us and how you can join our team!

Our Commitment to Inclusion & Belonging

At Copeland, we cultivate a strong sense of inclusion and belonging where individuals of all backgrounds, and with diverse perspectives, are embraced and treated fairly to enable a stronger workforce. Our employee resource groups play an important role in culture and community building at Copeland.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Copeland is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, religion, national origin, age, marital status, political affiliation, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, disability or protected veteran status. We are committed to providing a workplace free of any discrimination or harassment.

Where does automation earn trust, and where does a human still need to stay in the loop?

About Accelerate:
Accelerate is InMobi s AI-native, self-serve campaign management platform for SMBs, D2C brands, agencies and enterprise advertisers. An advertiser describes their brand and goals; Accelerate s agents plan, create, launch and optimize campaigns across ad platforms such as TikTok and OpenAI, with more supply integrations on the way.
We are building toward a fully autonomous marketing platform. The product team is organized by capability, not segment. This role sits on the demand side, reporting to the Group Product Manager, alongside Customer Experience Core (campaign creation, onboarding and activation).

About the role:
You will build Accelerate s payments and money infrastructure from zero. Every dollar or rupee an advertiser puts into Accelerate flows through what you build: how they fund their account, how spend is drawn down across ad platforms, how they are invoiced, refunded and taxed, and how we settle with suppliers.
There is no legacy system to inherit. You will define the wallet, the ledger behind it, and the integration with our third-party payments partner (Vyre), then own the revenue metrics that depend on them. Getting this right is what lets an SMB go from signup to live campaign in minutes, and what lets finance trust every number on the dashboard.
You will work with a Senior Product Associate on the pod, engineering, Central Design, and InMobi finance, tax and legal teams.
What you will own:
  • Advertiser wallet. A prepaid balance advertisers top up and Accelerate draws down as campaigns spend. Includes funding methods, auto-recharge, low-balance alerts, credit lines for larger accounts, and the rules for how a balance can and cannot be used.
  • Ledger and reconciliation. The source of truth for every credit, debit, hold, refund and adjustment. Spend reported by each ad platform must reconcile to the ledger, with clear handling for mismatches.
  • Payments integration. End-to-end integration with Vyre, our third-party payments partner: collections, payment methods, failures and retries, webhooks, and the fallback plan if a provider is down.
  • Billing, invoicing and tax. Invoices, receipts, GST, TDS on ad spend, and multi-currency handling as we add international advertisers.
  • Supplier settlement. How we pay out and reconcile with ad platforms, working with the business team that handles supplier contracts.
  • Segment needs. SMBs prepaying by card or UPI, agencies funding many client accounts from one place, and enterprise clients on invoiced terms.
  • Revenue metrics. Top-up conversion, payment success rate, time to first funded campaign, wallet balance retention, and reconciliation accuracy. Every revenue number in Accelerate s success framework depends on your system.
What we re looking for:
  • 6+ years of product management, with at least 3 years owning payments, wallets, billing or ledger systems.
  • You have built a payments or wallet system from scratch, or led its first major version. Scaling a mature system alone is not enough.
  • Deep understanding of double-entry ledgers, idempotency, reconciliation, refunds and chargebacks. You can sit with engineers and discuss failure modes, not just flows.
  • Hands-on experience integrating a third-party payment provider or aggregator end to end.
  • Working knowledge of Indian payments regulation and tax: RBI rules on prepaid instruments, GST, TDS. You know when to bring in legal and what to ask them.
  • You work AI-native (see How we work below). You prototype, write and reason with LLMs as part of your daily work.
  • Clear written communication. You can explain a ledger design to an engineer, a finance controller and an SMB owner, each in their own terms.
    Strong pluses
  • You built a wallet or stored-balance feature inside a non-fintech product, such as a marketplace, mobility, food delivery or SaaS platform.
  • Experience with ad-platform billing (prepaid, postpaid or credit-line models) or marketplace payouts.
  • Experience with cross-border payments, multi-currency balances or FX.
  • Experience with B2B billing for agencies or multi-entity accounts.
  • Some time as an engineer, or comfort reading API docs and querying data directly.
How we work:
Accelerate is an AI-native product, and we build it the AI-native way. Every PM on the demand side is expected to:
  • Prototype before you spec. Turn an idea into a clickable prototype with AI tools in hours, and test it with users and the team before writing requirements.
  • Write and think with LLMs. Draft PRDs, edge cases, test cases and analyses with an LLM as a working partner. Then apply your own judgment to what it gets wrong.
  • Hand off with less back-and-forth. Give engineering and design specs precise enough to build from, with prototypes and acceptance criteria attached, so fewer decisions get made in meetings.
  • Stay close to the data. Pull and analyze data yourself rather than waiting on a dashboard request.
  • Bring design sense. Care about the details of the customer experience and partner with design as a peer, not a requester. We will test this in the interview loop, not just ask about it.
Since 2007, InMobi has built the extraordinary. Beyond just technology. It has built a way of working.
Across 16 offices globally, through every pivot and breakthrough, one thing has remained constant: we are builders, dreamers, doers. We are fluid enough to move fast, grounded enough to own outcomes, and human enough to care deeply about the work and about one another.
Culture is at the core of that ethos. It has been co-created by the people who built this company and by those continuing to shape it every day. It lives in how we work, how decisions are made, how teams show up for one another, and how seriously we take the responsibility to build the best.

About Accelerate:
Accelerate is InMobi s AI-native, self-serve campaign management platform for SMBs, D2C brands, agencies and enterprise advertisers. An advertiser describes their brand and goals; Accelerate s agents plan, create, launch and optimize campaigns across ad platforms such as TikTok and OpenAI, with more supply integrations on the way.
We are building toward a fully autonomous marketing platform. This role sits on the demand side, reporting to the Group Product Manager for Customer Experience Core.

About the role:
You will own the heart of Accelerate: the experience that turns a brand s goals into a live, running campaign. That includes campaign creation, the chat interface advertisers use to work with our agents, and AI creative generation. You will make that one experience work for very different customers: an SMB owner launching a first campaign, an agency running dozens of client accounts, a mid-size advertiser scaling spend, and an enterprise team with approval processes. You will also take Accelerate beyond our own
app, through APIs for companies that want our capabilities without onboarding, and through bundled offerings inside SMB-heavy platforms such as Stripe, Razorpay and Shopify. This is a senior, high-ownership role. The product is agentic and LLM-driven, so you will shape not just screens but how the agent reasons, what it produces, and how we measure whether it is good.

What you will own:
  • Campaign creation, chat and creative generation. The hero surface where an advertiser s brand blueprint becomes a live campaign. You own the end-to-end flow, the conversation design, and the quality of what the agent produces.
  • Segment-specific journeys. One product that adapts to SMBs, agencies, mid-size advertisers and enterprise clients. Includes multi-account workflows for agencies and controls, approvals and roles for enterprise.
  • AI quality for your surfaces. Prompt and RAG design for brand context, eval sets that define good for a campaign plan or a creative, and quality gates that releases must pass. The Agentic AI pod owns platform-wide autonomy tiers and guardrails; you own whether your surfaces produce the right output.
  • APIs and headless access. A public API so partners and larger customers can create and manage campaigns without using our UI. You own the developer experience, docs and pricing model, working with engineering on the design.
  • Embedded distribution. Accelerate as a bundled offering inside platforms such as Stripe, Razorpay and Shopify. You shape the product side of these partnerships: the in-partner experience, account linking and the value proposition, working with the business team on the deals.
  • Metrics. Time from brief to live campaign, campaign launch rate, creative acceptance rate, eval pass rates, and adoption by segment and by channel (app, API, partner).
What we re looking for:
  • 6+ years of product management, with at least 2 years owning a B2B product used by multiple customer segments.
  • You have shipped an LLM-powered product to real users in production, not just a pilot or demo. You have dealt with hallucinations, latency, cost and quality regressions.
  • Hands-on understanding of RAG, prompt design, agentic workflows and evals. You have written eval sets yourself and used them to decide whether something ships.
  • Strong design sense. You can show work where you shaped the experience in detail, and you partner with designers as a peer.
  • You work AI-native (see How we work below). You prototype, write and reason with LLMs as part of your daily work.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and a wide scope. You can keep the hero surface moving while building the API and partnership tracks alongside it.
  • Clear written communication with engineers, designers, business partners and customers.
Strong pluses
  • Experience in martech, adtech or performance marketing products, or time as a performance marketer yourself.
  • Built or owned a public API, developer platform or partner app (for example, a Shopify app or a payment-platform integration).
  • Shipped a product that serves both self-serve SMBs and enterprise or agency accounts from one codebase.
  • Experience with generative creative: image, video or ad copy generation with brand-safety checks.
  • A portfolio or public writing showing your product and design thinking.
How we work
Accelerate is an AI-native product, and we build it the AI-native way. Every PM on the demand side is expected to:
  • Prototype before you spec. Turn an idea into a clickable prototype with AI tools in hours, and test it with users and the team before writing requirements.
  • Write and think with LLMs. Draft PRDs, edge cases, test cases, and analyses with an LLM as a working partner. Then apply your own judgment to what it gets wrong.
  • Hand off with less back-and-forth. Give engineering and design specs precise enough to build from, with prototypes and acceptance criteria attached, so fewer decisions get made in meetings.
  • Stay close to the data. Pull and analyze data yourself rather than waiting on a dashboard request.
  • Bring design sense. Care about the details of the customer experience and partner with design as a peer, not a requester. We will test this in the interview loop, not just ask about it.

Job Summary

In this role, you turn how a business works into a precise blueprint a tech team can build from. We call this systems thinking: seeing a business as connected parts (people, operations, rules, data and handoffs) and designing how they should work together. The role sits close to a product manager, but starts earlier and goes deeper: on the operations floor.

You will sit with operators, managers and finance teams, capture what really happens, and map it as a process. Then you will design the better version: the data it needs, the rules it must enforce, the screens people use, and what happens when something fails. Your output is the PRD, BRD and screen specs our engineers implement. You will do this work with AI as your main tool. Our Process Docs method runs inside Claude Code, and you will use it daily to capture, structure, review and refine documentation. This role suits someone early in their career who wants to learn how real businesses run and how good software is designed for them.

Key Responsibilities

  • Observe and capture. Visit client sites, shadow work and interview people. Record each activitys inputs, outputs, people, timing and problems, including the workarounds and exceptions nobody mentions at first.
  • Map processes. Turn observations into step-by-step flows with every handoff, decision point and exception path named. A new employee should be able to follow your map on day one.
  • Analyze and decide. Compare options, dig into the hard parts of a problem, and help settle the tech stack and implementation approach before design begins.
  • Write PRDs and BRDs. Translate processes into requirements with IDs, business rules, data entities and acceptance criteria. Design the improved process, not a digital copy of the old one.
  • Specify screens. For each screen, define entry points, layout, data shown, actions, validations, and empty, loading, error and restricted states.
  • Design for correctness. Define the source of truth for each balance and status. Spell out how the system handles concurrent users, duplicate requests, partial fulfilment, cancellations and integration failures.
  • Write the scope. Produce a self-contained scope document clients can read and sign off without opening anything else.
  • Review and close gaps. Audit documentation for completeness, consistency and depth. Turn every gap into a specific question someone can answer.
  • Stay with the build. Answer engineers questions, review shipped work against acceptance criteria, and keep the PRD in step with what was built.

Requirements

Mandatory Requirements

  • 0-2 years of work experience. Freshers with strong projects (in intern roles) are welcome.
  • A degree in engineering, computer science or business, or equivalent proof of ability. We care more about how you think than what you studied.
  • Strong critical thinking. You break a problem into parts, test assumptions, and spot what doesnt add up.
  • You think beyond the obvious. You look past the process as described to the exceptions, workarounds and knock-on effects behind it.
  • You ask sharp questions. In a room with a client, you ask the questions that reveal how the business really works: "Who decides that", "Why is it done this way", "What happens when this fails"
  • Strong communication, written and spoken. You can describe a process so someone who wasnt there understands it, and explain a design to a client and an engineer alike.
  • Curiosity to learn, by nature. When something is outside your territory, you dive in with confidence and interest rather than waiting to be taught.
  • Comfort reasoning about state and rules. Given "available = on-hand - held - reserved", you can trace balances through a sequence of actions without error.
  • Basic software building ability. You can build and run a small application with persistent storage, using any stack you can defend.
  • Hands-on use of AI coding tools, ideally Claude Code. You can direct an AI, check its output, and reject a wrong recommendation.
  • Ability to read API contracts, sequence flows and acceptance criteria.
  • Willingness to travel to client sites and spend time on factory floors, warehouses and offices.

Good to Have

  • Experience as an Associate Product Manager, or on a team building digital products. This is the strongest signal we look for. An internship in such a role counts.
  • Exposure to operations domains: procurement, inventory, warehousing, sales order management, logistics or finance.
  • An internship or project with a consulting, ERP or operations team.
  • Familiarity with ERPs or low-code platforms such as SAP, Tally, Zoho, Odoo or Mendix, and how they integrate with custom systems.
  • Understanding of transactions, idempotency, concurrency and audit trails in business software.
  • Working knowledge of data modelling: entities, relationships, keys and constraints. You can sketch a schema for orders, stock and dispatches.
  • Experience writing PRDs, user stories, wireframes or test cases.
  • Comfort with Markdown, Git and diagram tools.
  • Hindi, Gujarati or another regional language, for conversations on client sites.

What we care about

  • Reality over assumption. We document what actually happens, not what the SOP says. Workarounds and edge cases matter more than the happy path.
  • Honest gaps. "I dont know yet" written down beats a confident guess. We mark unknowns and turn them into answerable questions.
  • Specifics, not adjectives. "3-5 minutes per batch" beats "takes some time". Name the person, the system, the number.
  • Failure is part of the design. A good spec says what happens when the network drops, the request repeats, or two people act at once.
  • Accountability for AI output. AI makes us fast. You own every line it helps you produce, and you verify it.
  • Builds, not decks. Our work is done when an engineer can build from it without guessing.

About You

You are at the start of your career and hungry to learn how businesses really work.

Lead product thinking on integrations (for example, POS systems) and new AI features.
Accept releases against the agreed specs before they go live.
Numbers
Own a monthly product dashboard for each client: new customers by source, conversion, churn, revenue per customer and delivery against the quarterly outcomes.

Company Description

Purpose of the role

Bosch Mobility Platform and Solutions (MPS) builds software platforms and digital services for the mobility ecosystem: tolling and traffic, logistics and fleets, commerce and marketplaces, financial services, and the cloud and data platform that runs underneath them. MPS works with partners and customers across India, Europe and North America, and operates like a digital-native business inside Bosch.

Toll.OS is the open-road tolling and traffic platform of Bosch MPS for Indian highways. It combines RFID and FASTag reads, number-plate recognition, vehicle classification and sensors into one verified transaction, and it runs on a layered architecture from the roadside edge to back-office reconciliation. It is live on a national highway today and is designed to scale from one gantry to many corridors.

The Toll.OS play also covers intelligent traffic management and enforcement at junctions and corridors, and the integration of tolling with highway Advanced Traffic Management Systems (ATMS) as national highway authorities specify in their tenders. The Product Manager owns this play as a product: what is built, how it performs in the field, what it costs to run, and what it needs to win the next deployment.

Job Description

What the role owns

Product strategy and roadmap - Own and evolve the roadmap across tolling (multi-lane free flow and plaza software), intelligent traffic management and enforcement, and integration with highway ATMS. Sequence work by customer need, economics, certification effort and regulatory readiness.

Field learning into requirements - Work from live deployments: recognition accuracy, manual validation rate, reconciliation gaps, notice and dispute failures, incident root causes. Turn each pattern into a prioritised backlog item with an owner.

Recognition and sensor-fusion quality - Define accuracy and confidence targets across RFID, number-plate recognition, vehicle classification and other sensors. Work with engineering and AI teams on model, camera and edge decisions, and lead make-or-buy choices on components.

Interoperability, compliance and security - Ensure the product meets national interoperability specifications for electronic toll collection, RFID and equipment standards, certification requirements, data protection, audit logging and retention. Work with Legal and Compliance on regulatory change.

Tender and bid support - Own the technical content of responses to highway authority and concessionaire tenders: compliance matrices, equivalence of components, architecture and service-level proposals. Work with Finance on bid-versus-investment discipline.

Deployment and operations readiness - Define site readiness, integration with acquirer banks and payment networks, settlement and reconciliation, service-level design and acceptance criteria. Hand over cleanly to operations and keep the live KPIs visible.

Unit economics - Own cost per passage and cost per plaza, and shape transaction-fee and service models with Finance, so the product stays competitive in price-led tenders.

Ecosystem and partners - Work with highway authorities, concessionaires, acquirer banks, system integrators and hardware vendors. Work with the Global Partner Manager on technology and supplier partnerships.

Platform and data integration - Publish passage and vehicle events into the Mobility Prism platform so the same vehicle can be understood across tolling, traffic and other services, within consent and data protection rules.

Team and ways of working - Guide the product owners and engineering squads working on Toll.OS using agile (SAFe) practices, and build the product-management discipline of the team through coaching and clear decision records

How the role is measured

The role is accountable for business outcomes, not only for product documentation. Effectiveness is assessed on:

Recognition accuracy and share of passages verified without manual review

Time from field issue to product fix

Cost per passage and cost per plaza trend

Technical compliance rate and win rate on tenders the role supported

Deployment lead time from contract to go-live

Reconciliation and settlement accuracy with acquirer banks

Number of corridors and plazas running on the standard product

Quality of field feedback captured into the roadmap

Qualifications

Who we are looking for

Education

Bachelor's degree in engineering (electronics, electrical, computer science, civil or transportation); a master's degree or MBA is an advantage.

Experience

8 to 12+ years in product management, systems engineering or programme leadership in intelligent transport systems, electronic toll collection, smart-city or transport technology, payments infrastructure or computer-vision based systems.

Has owned a product or system through design, certification, field deployment and operation, and has seen how it behaves when real traffic arrives.

Experience in public-sector or regulated procurement (tenders, compliance matrices, service-level and performance guarantees) is strongly preferred.

Domain and technical knowledge

Electronic toll collection: FASTag and national electronic toll collection specifications, RFID standards, acquirer and issuer roles, settlement and reconciliation.

Number-plate recognition, computer vision and sensor fusion; understanding of accuracy metrics, confidence cascades and model monitoring.

Edge computing, plaza and back-office systems, and integration through APIs; familiarity with traffic management and enforcement systems is an advantage.

Certification, equipment standards, cybersecurity and data protection as they apply to roadside systems.

Able to read an architecture, challenge a design and translate field problems into engineering requirements.

Commercial skills

Unit economics, pricing and service-level commercials; comfortable with a P&L view of a product.

Negotiation and relationship skills with authorities, banks and vendors.

Personal attributes

Strong ownership and bias to action; comfortable operating with ambiguity in a new business.

Field-minded: willing to spend time at sites and with operations teams, with regular domestic travel.

Clear structured communicator, in writing and in the room, who can explain a technical trade-off to a senior stakeholder.

Integrity and discretion when working with public authorities and sensitive data.

Collaborative leader who influences without formal authority across engineering, business and partners.

Additional Information

Who the role works with

Product Area Leader for the UtilizationStack (MPS/PAZ)

Engineering, AI and DevSecOps teams

Delivery, site and operations teams

Bid and tender team, and the Global Partner Manager

Finance, Legal and Compliance

Regional business leadership (MPS/RBR)

Highway authorities, concessionaires, acquirer banks, system integrators and vendors

Product owners for Mobility Prism and for financial services built on toll data

How to read this role

This is a product-ownership role with business accountability, not a project management or pure engineering role. The ideal candidate combines systems depth, field experience, commercial judgement and the ability to win trust with authorities and partners.

DESCRIPTION

Amazon Supply Chain Services (ASCS), which includes Multichannel Commerce Fulfillment (MCCF), lets merchants use Amazon’s fulfilment and logistics network to reach customers wherever they shop: their own websites, social commerce, other marketplaces and wholesale. Our vision is to enable every entrepreneur in the world to reach every customer in the world through every channel they can imagine. Through Multi-Channel Fulfillment (MCF), Buy with Prime (BwP), Multi-Channel Distribution (MCD) and Warehousing & Logistics, merchants keep products in stock, ship faster and more reliably, and lower their costs. For over 20 years Amazon has helped small and medium-sized businesses grow on Amazon; ASCS is how we help merchants of every size grow beyond it.

As ASCS scales, how merchants find, choose and get more out of it matters as much as what it offers. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager–Technical (Sr. PMT) to shape how ASCS grows with merchants: understanding why merchants who would benefit are not yet using our services, building the products and platforms that change that, and proving what actually moves the business. You will pair strategic vision with hands-on execution, working across engineering, business, finance and data science teams to build products fundamental to Amazon’s future.

Key job responsibilities
> Product strategy & direction: Continuously assess the needs of our customers and partners in defining and evolving the product and business strategy. Identify where ASCS services create the most value for merchants and translate those insights into a clear, differentiated product direction across marketing and pricing surfaces.
> Roadmap planning: Deliver world-class innovation in features, usability, and performance in a consistent release cadence. Be the internal and external authority for your program, driving value-based prioritisation from concept to launch to maximise ROI.
> Requirements definition: Develop comprehensive product plans incorporating merchant needs, competitive context, and business objectives. Produce high-quality requirements docs and manage scope to deliver key capabilities on time.
> Technical collaboration: Partner with engineering to craft BRDs, influence the design and architecture of technical solutions, and make informed trade-off decisions that balance merchant impact with implementation complexity.
> AI & productivity leverage: Apply AI tools to meaningfully accelerate product development from drafting and iterating on requirement document, merchant-facing messaging, to customer research, modelling pricing scenarios, and generating campaign briefs. You will actively identify where AI can compress timelines and improve output quality across the product lifecycle, and serve as a proponent of AI adoption within your cross-functional teams.

A day in the life
> Collaborate with GTM, Sales, User Research, Tech, Finance, and Operations to define strategy, vision, and features for MCF and ASCS adoption.
> Own the product backlog and BRDs across marketing and pricing workstreams; prioritize and make feature trade-offs that maximize merchant adoption and ROI.
> Deliver products end-to-end across Engineering, Legal, Information Security, UX, and Finance from concept through launch.
> Design, launch, and iterate on lifecycle automation and targeted campaigns to engage and convert unmanaged merchants at scale.

About the team

ASCS helps merchants of every size reach customers on any channel through Multi-Channel Fulfillment, Buy with Prime, Multi-Channel Distribution and Warehousing & Logistics. The ASCS Monetisation team owns how this business earns while keeping merchants’ trust. We set what merchants pay through rate cards, fees, discounts, incentives and negotiated pricing. We make merchants whole when inventory or orders are lost, damaged or returned. And we decide how merchants are invoiced and collected from, extending flexible payment terms without avoidable bad debt. Every decision must be calculated correctly, posted accurately, explained clearly and measured for real impact.

About Accelerate:
Accelerate is InMobi's AI-native, self-serve campaign management platform for SMBs, D2C brands, agencies and enterprise advertisers. An advertiser describes their brand and goals; Accelerate's agents plan, create, launch and optimize campaigns across ad platforms such as TikTok and OpenAI, with more supply integrations on the way.
We are building toward a fully autonomous marketing platform. This role sits on the demand side, reporting to the Group Product Manager for Customer Experience Core.

About the role:
You will own the heart of Accelerate: the experience that turns a brand's goals into a live, running campaign. That includes campaign creation, the chat interface advertisers use to work with our agents, and AI creative generation. You will make that one experience work for very different customers: an SMB owner launching a first campaign, an agency running dozens of client accounts, a mid-size advertiser scaling spend, and an enterprise team with approval processes. You will also take Accelerate beyond our own
app, through APIs for companies that want our capabilities without onboarding, and through bundled offerings inside SMB-heavy platforms such as Stripe, Razorpay and Shopify. This is a senior, high-ownership role. The product is agentic and LLM-driven, so you will shape not just screens but how the agent reasons, what it produces, and how we measure whether it is good.

What you will own:

Campaign creation, chat and creative generation. The hero surface where an advertiser's brand blueprint becomes a live campaign. You own the end-to-end flow, the conversation design, and the quality of what the agent produces.
Segment-specific journeys. One product that adapts to SMBs, agencies, mid-size advertisers and enterprise clients. Includes multi-account workflows for agencies and controls, approvals and roles for enterprise.
AI quality for your surfaces. Prompt and RAG design for brand context, eval sets that define "good" for a campaign plan or a creative, and quality gates that releases must pass. The Agentic AI pod owns platform-wide autonomy tiers and guardrails; you own whether your surfaces produce the right output.
APIs and headless access. A public API so partners and larger customers can create and manage campaigns without using our UI. You own the developer experience, docs and pricing model, working with engineering on the design.
Embedded distribution. Accelerate as a bundled offering inside platforms such as Stripe, Razorpay and Shopify. You shape the product side of these partnerships: the in-partner experience, account linking and the value proposition, working with the business team on the deals.
Metrics. Time from brief to live campaign, campaign launch rate, creative acceptance rate, eval pass rates, and adoption by segment and by channel (app, API, partner).

What we're looking for:

6+ years of product management, with at least 2 years owning a B2B product used by multiple customer segments.
You have shipped an LLM-powered product to real users in production, not just a pilot or demo. You have dealt with hallucinations, latency, cost and quality regressions.
Hands-on understanding of RAG, prompt design, agentic workflows and evals. You have written eval sets yourself and used them to decide whether something ships.
Strong design sense. You can show work where you shaped the experience in detail, and you partner with designers as a peer.
You work AI-native (see "How we work" below). You prototype, write and reason with LLMs as part of your daily work.
Comfortable with ambiguity and a wide scope. You can keep the hero surface moving while building the API and partnership tracks alongside it.
Clear written communication with engineers, designers, business partners and customers.

Strong pluses

Experience in martech, adtech or performance marketing products, or time as a performance marketer yourself.
Built or owned a public API, developer platform or partner app (for example, a Shopify app or a payment-platform integration).
Shipped a product that serves both self-serve SMBs and enterprise or agency accounts from one codebase.
Experience with generative creative: image, video or ad copy generation with brand-safety checks.
A portfolio or public writing showing your product and design thinking.

How we work
Accelerate is an AI-native product, and we build it the AI-native way. Every PM on the demand side is expected to:

Prototype before you spec. Turn an idea into a clickable prototype with AI tools in hours, and test it with users and the team before writing requirements.
Write and think with LLMs. Draft PRDs, edge cases, test cases, and analyses with an LLM as a working partner. Then apply your own judgment to what it gets wrong.
Hand off with less back-and-forth. Give engineering and design specs precise enough to build from, with prototypes and acceptance criteria attached, so fewer decisions get made in meetings.
Stay close to the data. Pull and analyze data yourself rather than waiting on a dashboard request.
Bring design sense. Care about the details of the customer experience and partner with design as a peer, not a requester. We will test this in the interview loop, not just ask about it.

Since 2007, InMobi has built the extraordinary. Beyond just technology. It has built a way of working.

Across 16 offices globally, through every pivot and breakthrough, one thing has remained constant: we are builders, dreamers, doers. We are fluid enough to move fast, grounded enough to own outcomes, and human enough to care deeply about the work and about one another.

Culture is at the core of that ethos. It has been co-created by the people who built this company and by those continuing to shape it every day. It lives in how we work, how decisions are made, how teams show up for one another, and how seriously we take the responsibility to build the best.

This is a place where ambition and belonging occupy the same space. Where the bar is high and the support is real. Where freedom comes with trust, and trust comes with accountability. Where you are valued not only for what you do, but for the perspective, judgment and humanity you bring to the work. Where you will be challenged by the work and supported by the communities, passions and experiences that shape who you are beyond your role.

If this sounds like the place you have been looking for, join us.

About Accelerate:
Accelerate is InMobi's AI-native, self-serve campaign management platform for SMBs, D2C brands, agencies and enterprise advertisers. An advertiser describes their brand and goals; Accelerate's agents plan, create, launch and optimize campaigns across ad platforms such as TikTok and OpenAI, with more supply integrations on the way.
We are building toward a fully autonomous marketing platform. The product team is organized by capability, not segment. This role sits on the demand side, reporting to the Group Product Manager, alongside Customer Experience Core (campaign creation, onboarding and activation).

About the role:
You will build Accelerate's payments and money infrastructure from zero. Every dollar or rupee an advertiser puts into Accelerate flows through what you build: how they fund their account, how spend is drawn down across ad platforms, how they are invoiced, refunded and taxed, and how we settle with suppliers.
There is no legacy system to inherit. You will define the wallet, the ledger behind it, and the integration with our third-party payments partner (Vyre), then own the revenue metrics that depend on them. Getting this right is what lets an SMB go from signup to live campaign in minutes, and what lets finance trust every number on the dashboard.
You will work with a Senior Product Associate on the pod, engineering, Central Design, and InMobi finance, tax and legal teams.

What you will own:

Advertiser wallet. A prepaid balance advertisers top up and Accelerate draws down as campaigns spend. Includes funding methods, auto-recharge, low-balance alerts, credit lines for larger accounts, and the rules for how a balance can and cannot be used.
Ledger and reconciliation. The source of truth for every credit, debit, hold, refund and adjustment. Spend reported by each ad platform must reconcile to the ledger, with clear handling for mismatches.
Payments integration. End-to-end integration with Vyre, our third-party payments partner: collections, payment methods, failures and retries, webhooks, and the fallback plan if a provider is down.
Billing, invoicing and tax. Invoices, receipts, GST, TDS on ad spend, and multi-currency handling as we add international advertisers.
Supplier settlement. How we pay out and reconcile with ad platforms, working with the business team that handles supplier contracts.
Segment needs. SMBs prepaying by card or UPI, agencies funding many client accounts from one place, and enterprise clients on invoiced terms.
Revenue metrics. Top-up conversion, payment success rate, time to first funded campaign, wallet balance retention, and reconciliation accuracy. Every revenue number in Accelerate's success framework depends on your system.

6+ years of product management, with at least 3 years owning payments, wallets, billing or ledger systems.
You have built a payments or wallet system from scratch, or led its first major version. Scaling a mature system alone is not enough.
Deep understanding of double-entry ledgers, idempotency, reconciliation, refunds and chargebacks. You can sit with engineers and discuss failure modes, not just flows.
Hands-on experience integrating a third-party payment provider or aggregator end to end.
Working knowledge of Indian payments regulation and tax: RBI rules on prepaid instruments, GST, TDS. You know when to bring in legal and what to ask them.
You work AI-native (see "How we work" below). You prototype, write and reason with LLMs as part of your daily work.
Clear written communication. You can explain a ledger design to an engineer, a finance controller and an SMB owner, each in their own terms.

You built a wallet or stored-balance feature inside a non-fintech product, such as a marketplace, mobility, food delivery or SaaS platform.
Experience with ad-platform billing (prepaid, postpaid or credit-line models) or marketplace payouts.
Experience with cross-border payments, multi-currency balances or FX.
Experience with B2B billing for agencies or multi-entity accounts.
Some time as an engineer, or comfort reading API docs and querying data directly.

About Jupiter
Jupiter is a money app for people who are building their lives in India. From one app you can open a savings account with our partner bank, pay on UPI, save towards goals in Pots, borrow, buy insurance, invest, and see where your money actually goes. Our Edge+ CSB Bank RuPay credit card works on UPI and earns Jewels, our rewards currency, on the brands people already shop with.
We are a product company at heart. We obsess over small details, we read what customers tell us, and we would rather do fewer things properly than many things badly.
Why this role exists
AI is already part of how Jupiter works. Our product team uses an in-house assistant that reads our Confluence, Figma, Amplitude, Databricks and support tickets to answer questions and draft PRDs, right inside Slack. Engineering has a bot that turns a Jira ticket into a draft pull request. Marketing has a creative studio that designs ads, critiques its own work against a checklist and tells us what every run cost.
Those started as tools for us. The next step is bigger: putting AI in front of customers in a product that handles their money, where a confident wrong answer is not a small bug. We are looking for a PM who wants to own that problem, with the judgement to know where AI helps and the discipline to prove it before it ships.
What you will do
Find the problems worth solving with AI. Explaining a declined payment, making sense of a card bill, help that actually closes the ticket, a Money tab that answers questions in plain words. You will also say no to the ideas where a better screen would do the job.
Own products end to end. Problem, PRD, evals, launch, and the numbers after launch. You stay with it until it works for customers, not until it is merged.
Write the evals before the feature. Define what good looks like with real examples, build the test sets with engineering, and decide the score that is good enough to ship. When the model changes, you know within a day whether things got better or worse.
Design for the moments AI gets it wrong. What the assistant says when it does not know, when it hands over to a person, and how a customer corrects it. These moments decide whether people trust us.
Keep it safe and compliant. Work with compliance, risk and our partner banks so everything we build respects RBI guidelines, the DPDP Act and our partners' policies. Customer data stays where it belongs.
Treat cost and speed as product decisions. Know what each conversation costs, pick the right model for each job, and cut what does not earn its keep.
Raise the bar for the whole team. Help other PMs, designers and analysts use AI well in their own work, and keep improving the internal tools they already rely on.
Your first 90 days
By day 30: you use Jupiter every day, have read a few hundred support conversations, have sat with ops and compliance, and know our internal AI tools by using them.
By day 60: you have picked one customer problem, made the case for it with real data, and put a working prototype in front of colleagues.
By day 90: you have an eval set, a launch plan with guardrails, and a small rollout to real customers with one clear success metric.

Have 4 to 8 years in product, with at least one AI or ML product shipped to real users. A demo does not count; something people used does.
Can explain in plain words how language models fail (making things up, prompt injection, behaviour shifting between model versions) and how you would design around each.
Are comfortable writing prompts, reading a model's outputs in bulk and spotting the pattern in what went wrong.
Use data without being asked. You can write SQL, build a funnel in Amplitude, and tell a real change from noise.
Write clearly. Your PRDs are short, specific and something an engineer can build from.
Care about the person on the other side of the screen, especially when the subject is their money.

Experience in fintech, payments, lending or another regulated space.
You have built with the Claude or OpenAI APIs yourself, even on a side project.
Hands-on time with retrieval (RAG), agents that use tools, or eval tooling.
You can sketch a flow in Figma before a designer picks it up.

About Tekion:

Positively disrupting an industry that has not seen any innovation in over 50 years, Tekion has challenged the paradigm with the first and fastest cloud-native automotive platform. Our platform spans the Automotive Retail Cloud (ARC) for retailers, the Automotive Enterprise Cloud (AEC) for manufacturers and other large automotive enterprises, and the Automotive Partner Cloud (APC) for technology and industry partners. Tekion connects the entire automotive retail ecosystem through one seamless platform, using cutting-edge technology, big data, machine learning, and AI to bring together vehicle manufacturers, dealerships, and consumers. Tekion employs close to 3,000 people across North America, Asia, and Europe.

About the Role:

Tekion connects dealerships - the businesses that sell and service vehicles - with the automakers that build those vehicles, such as General Motors, Honda, or Ford. Across the industry these automakers are referred to as OEMs (Original Equipment Manufacturers). The software on each side needs to exchange information automatically and reliably: vehicle orders, inventory, repair records, customer details, and much more. The software that makes this exchange happen is called integration. We are seeking a driven, technically curious Product Manager I to join our Integrations team. You will take ownership of one integration pattern - a family of similar integrations that share the same shape (for example, all the integrations that send vehicle service and repair data to automakers). Your mission is to make every integration in that family measurably healthy and best-in-class, shift more of its delivery from manual building to AI-assisted building, and make sure dealerships actually adopt and benefit from it. This is a hands-on role for an early-career product manager who is comfortable with technical concepts, motivated by measurable outcomes, and excited to help modernize how a decades-old industry connects its software. You will work closely with Engineering, Design, and senior product managers, who will guide and mentor you as you grow into full ownership of your integration pattern.

What You’ll Do:

• Keep your integrations healthy and best-in-class: Define what “good” looks like for your integration pattern, measure it in our Integration Platform (Tekion’s internal health-monitoring system), and drive coverage, reliability, and quality up across all your integrations - benchmarking each against the best competing product in the market.
• Win on AI-powered delivery: Shift your pattern from hand-built integrations toward ones generated with Tekion’s AI-assisted build tools (internally, APC Studio), help sharpen the AI tools you depend on, and own a complete, living set of requirements that any engineering team can build from.
• Drive revenue through OEM certifications: Lead integration patterns toward successful OEM certification so OEM-approved integrations can be adopted by dealers at scale. Drive adoption and reduce support load: Make your integrations easy to install and switch on, raise dealership uptake where it is low, and reduce support tickets by tracking and fixing root causes.
• Partner across teams: Translate the needs of dealers, automakers, and partners into clear requirements, and work day-to-day with Engineering, Design, Support, and Go-to-Market teams to deliver, launch, and measure impact.

• Around 6+ years of product management experience, or equivalent experience in a technical product, integration, API, or platform role.
• Exposure to integrations, APIs, or platform and marketplace products, with the ability to read technical documentation and discuss APIs, webhooks, and data flows with engineers. (An API is a defined way for two systems to exchange data; a webhook is an automatic notification one system sends another when something happens. You do not need to write code.)
• A strong bias toward measurable outcomes, with comfort using dashboards, metrics, and data to set targets and track progress.
• Clear writing skills - the ability to turn messy, ambiguous requirements into crisp specifications and user stories. • Curiosity about AI and how it can automate technical work, plus the drive to improve the tools you use.
• Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work with both technical and non-technical audiences.
• The ability to manage ambiguity, prioritize effectively, and make thoughtful trade-offs in a fast-paced environment.
• A bachelor’s degree in business, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to Have:

• Familiarity with the automotive retail world - dealerships, the Dealer Management System (DMS, the core software a dealership runs its business on), or automaker (OEM) certification programs.

• Modernize an industry: Help modernize how an entire industry connects its software, moving from slow, hand-built integrations to a fast, AI-powered delivery model.
